en.headline: Justice chief says law remains option on minors' social media
en.dek: Paul Lam said legislation to regulate how children use social media is one option under study, after the policy address ordered a task force led by his department.
body: Secretary for Justice Paul Lam Ting-kwok said introducing legislation to regulate minors' use of social media remains among the options being examined, after the latest Policy Address ordered a dedicated task force under the Department of Justice.

Speaking to the South China Morning Post and other media on Wednesday, Mr Lam dismissed concerns that such measures would necessarily infringe on individual rights, saying the aim was to protect children from online harms including pornography. The interdepartmental group is to review risks tied to minors' use of social media and artificial intelligence platforms and assess whether legislative or administrative changes are needed.

The Chief Executive announced the task force in the Policy Address on 16 September. Mr Lam has previously said any proposal would be judged against Hong Kong conditions, that education measures from the Education Bureau form part of a multi-pronged approach, and that the public would be consulted before new rules were introduced.

zh.headline: 林定國：立法規管未成年用社交媒體仍是選項
zh.dek: 律政司司長表示，施政報告提出由律政司牽頭成立專責小組後，立法規管兒童使用社交媒體仍屬研究範圍之一。
body: 律政司司長林定國表示，立法規管未成年人使用社交媒體，仍是當局研究中的其中一個選項。行政長官在最新一份《施政報告》提出，由律政司牽頭成立專責小組，檢視有關問題。
林定國周三接受《南華早報》及其他傳媒訪問時說，有關措施不一定構成對個人權利的侵犯，目標是保護兒童免受色情等網上有害內容影響。跨部門小組將檢視未成年人使用社交媒體及人工智能平台的風險，並評估是否需要立法或行政措施。
行政長官於9月16日《施政報告》宣布成立該小組。林定國較早前亦表明，任何建議都要結合香港實際情況，教育局的教育工作屬多管齊下的一部分，推出新措施前會諮詢公眾。
